facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage fell from 6.43x total debt to EBITDA at the end of 2024 to 5.90x at the end of 2025 and 4.19x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net leverage moved from 6.06x to 5.52x, which becomes -10.10x pro forma for the Aerospace sale of 2026-03-16, and then to a net cash position. The first step came from EBITDA rising from USD 61.91 million to USD 79.51 million faster than debt rose from USD 398.12 million to USD 469.17 million. The second came from the Aerospace sale, which lifted cash to USD 1,158.54 million while the revolver was repaid and debt fell to USD 397.14 million. The year-end ratios set debt that funded the whole group against continuing EBITDA only, so they overstate the leverage of the business that remains, and the last-twelve-month ratio is flattered by the asbestos benefit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6, 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 88–90, 136; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C08

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: EBITDA to cash interest paid improved from 3.31x in 2024 to 4.24x in 2025 and 4.98x on the last twelve months. Interest paid is gross: interest income of USD 23.9 million on the sale proceeds in the nine months of 2026 exceeds interest expense of USD 13.50 million, which is why the covenant interest-cover test prints as not applicable. Interest income is outside EBITDA, so the cover ratio is unaffected by it, but the net interest burden is negative only while the proceeds stay invested; deploying the cash into acquisitions or buybacks, or a fall in rates, would remove part of that income. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation C04

- High: The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA bridge, so EBITDA is derived from operating profit and continuing depreciation and amortization for every period. The last-twelve-month figure includes a net asbestos benefit of USD 35.80 million from the fourth quarter of 2025, which lifts it from USD 58.94 million. Leverage conclusions therefore need the sensitivity beside the reported ratio; management's adjusted EBITDA definition and the earnings release schedules would close the gap. They cannot support or replace the derived leverage, and covenant capacity cannot be inferred without the executed credit agreement and its amendments. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; calculation C07 - Medium: Year-end debt at 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31 funded the whole group including Aerospace, while EBITDA and the segment figures cover continuing operations only, so the two year-end leverage ratios overstate the leverage of the remaining business. facts.text: - Customer and input-cost exposure shows first in segment margins. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a lower level is that the revolver is repaid, no net debt has been added, covenant leverage is 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum, the dividend is USD 0.04 per share a quarter, buybacks and dividends absorbed 7.52% of cash, management lists repaying debt including the notes among possible uses, and no priming, exchange or related-party transaction is disclosed. The strongest evidence for a higher level is the USD 101.10 million of buybacks before the sale closed, two authorisation increases in four months, broad discretion over the proceeds and a further fall of 1.00% in shares outstanding after quarter end. If the proxy statement shows an independent board and no controlling holder, and the executed documents restrict distributions and new debt tightly, the level would move to low. It would move to high if the cash is spent on debt-funded acquisitions, special distributions or a much larger buyback, or if the credit agreement is amended to widen restricted-payment capacity. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 53, 55, 57; calculation C06; calculation C11

facts.label: Governance view
facts.text: Overall, Trimas presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The risk level is driven by USD 101.10 million of buybacks before the sale closed, USD 87.13 million of buybacks and dividends in nine months of 2026 and a management plan that leaves the use of USD 1,158.54 million of cash open, because cash that is returned or spent on acquisitions is no longer available to the holders of the USD 400.00 million unsecured notes, which implies that creditor risk moves with how much of the cash is returned or spent. Countervailing evidence is the repaid revolver, no net new debt, reported total net leverage of 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum and the absence of any extraction, related-party or liability management event. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and any announced acquisition. Business & governance completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 53; calculation C06; calculation C12

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a stronger view is that the company has net cash of USD 761.40 million, no maturity before April 2029, reported covenant leverage of 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum and cost savings of about USD 15.00 million a year still to come, which would make adequate too cautious if the cash stays on the balance sheet. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that without the asbestos benefit total debt is 6.74x EBITDA and interest income supplies 68.09% of pre-tax income. The view would improve if EBITDA without one-off items reaches the reported level on its own, if the notes are repaid or the cash is retained, or if Specialty Products returns to a positive margin. It would weaken if cash is spent on debt-funded acquisitions or a much larger buyback, if the revolver is drawn, if Packaging organic growth turns negative, or if the cylinder losses of the third quarter recur. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27, 53, 55, 57; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C08

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Trimas makes dispensing and closure systems for consumer products, life sciences and industrial customers, which are 82.94% of net sales, and steel cylinders for industrial gas, health care and defense uses, which are 17.06%. The Aerospace group, which was 38.04% of pre-sale group net sales, was sold in March 2026 and the bag-in-box product line followed in November 2026. Many Packaging products are designed to customer specifications, and the footprint across North America, Europe and Asia lets customers buy locally, which supports retention but also exposes the company to the buying patterns of large consumer brands. The credit linkage is that the remaining business is smaller but steadier: Packaging net sales rose in 2024, in 2025 and in nine months of 2026 while the cylinder unit has swung with industrial demand, so debt service rests on one platform with two end-market risks. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is spread across consumer, life sciences and industrial customers but is cyclical at the edges. Packaging net sales grew 5.8% in nine months of 2026, with life sciences up USD 13.5 million and dispensing for beauty and personal care up USD 4.4 million, partly offset by a USD 5.1 million fall in other consumer goods, and organic growth reached 8.2% in the third quarter. The cylinder unit's sales rose 9.5% on industrial demand and market share gains after a demand trough from late 2023 to early 2025. Pricing power is limited: price increases generally lag input costs, escalator clauses exist only in some contracts, and each segment has a customer above 10% of its revenue, so order changes by one buyer can move segment results. Recent growth supports near-term revenue, but contract duration and renewal data are not supplied, so visibility beyond the next year and any pricing cushion against cost shocks are not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 41–42, 46–47

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins have held in Packaging and not in Specialty Products. Packaging gross margin was 23.4% in nine months of 2026 against 24.1%, after USD 1.9 million of higher realignment costs from closing one facility, having already fallen in 2025 on higher input costs including tariffs, and its segment margin was 11.98% against 13.17%. In Specialty Products, a USD 2.1 million inventory-count charge, machine downtime and labour inefficiency cut the gross margin from 9.0% to 5.5%. Resin, steel and aluminum are the largest purchases and price increases lag cost increases, so a cost shock first hits margin and then cash conversion. Corporate expense fell to USD 26.50 million from USD 44.64 million, partly because a USD 8.0 million asbestos charge in the prior year did not repeat. Packaging segment margin held between 12.72% and 13.30% across 2023 to 2025, so margins have been defended through volume and cost swings so far, but a cost shock in resin or steel would pass through to EBITDA with a delay. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 55, 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 41–43, 45, 47–49; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is low and flexible: cash capital expenditure of continuing operations was USD 17.54 million over the last twelve months, 2.59% of net sales, against USD 31.69 million in 2025, so EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest 4.06x. Against that, receivables rose USD 46.32 million in nine months and days sales outstanding rose twelve days because sales grew with customers that pay more slowly, and realignment, severance and system costs continue. Taxes on the sale gain, not operations, drove the nine-month operating cash outflow. EBITDA therefore appears to convert into cash for debt service, but the conversion of the remaining business cannot be measured until a continuing cash flow statement exists. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate: no single competitor matches the whole Packaging range, but Amcor, Aptar, Silgan, Greif, Bericap and smaller Asian producers compete in each product line, so the main margin risk is the lag in passing on cost increases rather than a stated price war. Buyer power is high for the large consumer brands that are the main customers, because the company says they may seek lower prices, different payment terms or local supply, and each segment has a customer above 10% of its revenue. Supplier power is low to moderate: resins are commodities with several suppliers, while steel is bought from mills and service centers and has had supply and pricing challenges, so supplier terms matter less than the lag in passing costs on. The threat of substitutes and of new entrants is not established from the materials supplied; the company notes only that customers may diversify their supply base and that sustainability goals push design toward less material. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 16, 27

facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Economic and political factors are material to credit; social and technological factors are not a primary driver on the materials supplied. facts.text: The credit supports are liquidity, the absence of maturities before 2029 and a margin-stable packaging platform; the constraints are the small earnings base, interest income dependence and an open financial policy. facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are life sciences growth, third-quarter organic growth of 8.2% in Packaging and realignment savings of more than USD 10 million in 2026 that rise to about USD 15.00 million annualised, with management saying the third quarter did not yet reflect them. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most credible downside is a policy-led one, not an operating collapse. If management spends most of the sale cash on acquisitions and buybacks while consumer demand softens and resin, steel or tariff costs outrun pricing, Packaging gross margin would fall further from the 23.4% of nine months 2026 and the cylinder unit would keep losing money, as in the third quarter. EBITDA would then move toward the USD 58.94 million that remains without the asbestos benefit, interest income would fall by about USD 3.90 million a year for every USD 100.00 million deployed, and total debt to EBITDA would stand at 6.74x even with no new debt. If acquisitions or buybacks were funded with the revolver, secured debt would rank ahead of the notes and borrowing capacity of USD 203.00 million, already limited by leverage tests, could shrink as covenant EBITDA falls. The notes would face refinancing in April 2029 at a lower rating on a smaller earnings base. Management levers are cutting buybacks, lowering capital expenditure from a low base and using the cash to repay the notes. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months, because cash alone covers the notes 2.90 times; distress would need a large cash outflow and a deep earnings fall together. The first observable signals are a falling cash balance, a drawn revolver, negative Packaging organic growth and repeated cylinder losses. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Trimas presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity that covers the notes 2.90 times and a margin-stable Packaging franchise, but credit quality is constrained by a small earnings base of USD 94.74 million that includes a one-off benefit, earnings that lean on interest income, and an open capital allocation policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but not fully assessable, because EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest 4.06x while free cash flow of the continuing business is not stated. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how much cash is retained until April 2029 and on EBITDA without one-off items. The primary downside path is a cash- or revolver-funded acquisition or buyback program at the same time as cylinder losses and input-cost pressure. Further analysis would require a continuing cash flow statement, management's adjusted EBITDA, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and sector benchmarks. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: use of the sale cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how much cash is retained until April 2029 and on EBITDA without one-off items. The primary downside path is a cash- or revolver-funded acquisition or buyback program at the same time as cylinder losses and input-cost pressure. Further analysis would require a continuing cash flow statement, management's adjusted EBITDA, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and sector benchmarks. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: use of the sale cash.

spans.text: ## Request

Trimas Corp (issuer id trs-842633; reporting entity TriMas Corporation) as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway, scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit. The information cutoff is 2026-11-18, the current period is the third quarter of 2026 and the comparison period is fiscal 2025. The run settings supply no portfolio, peer, market quote or legal-document inputs.

No analysis from another module was supplied; this is the first module in the run. No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five filings support a credit snapshot of Trimas Corp as of 2026-11-18, but only the 2025 annual report and the three 2026 quarterly reports show the business that remains after the Aerospace sale, so creditor metrics must use them. The sale closed in March 2026, and the 2025 annual report already presents Aerospace as discontinued operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6

The 2024 annual report still includes Aerospace in continuing results, so its sales of USD 925.01 million are not comparable with the later filings, and the 2025 annual report restates that year to USD 630.80 million. The executed credit agreement and notes indenture are not supplied, so covenant terms can be read only as the quarterly reports summarise them. Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit can proceed, with no proxy statement for board and compensation detail.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 145–147; calculation C01

- Medium: The executed credit agreement, its December 2025 and March 2026 amendments and the notes indenture are not supplied. Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control and Recovery & fulcrum need the executed documents; Fundamental credit can quote the reported covenant tests but cannot test their definitions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 17

- Low: The 2024 annual report includes Aerospace in continuing results, while the 2025 annual report restates 2024 and 2023 without it. For both years the first reported sales exceed the restated sales by exactly the Aerospace segment sales, so the two reports reconcile; 2022 exists only on the old perimeter and the 2024 segment detail cannot describe the continuing business.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C01; calculation C02

- Low: The third-quarter earnings release was furnished on 2026-10-29 but is not supplied. The third quarterly report states that management lowered operating profit by USD 2.8 million after the release, so the release would show a higher figure than the quarterly report; any adjusted measure that appears only in the release is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 60

- Low: The Aerospace sale price is reported three ways: about USD 1.45 billion in the 2025 annual report, approximately USD 1,456.9 million in the first two quarterly reports while adjustments were pending, and approximately USD 1,457.1 million in the third quarterly report after adjustments. The third quarterly report controls; the difference between the last two is USD 0.2 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C03

- Low: The 2025 annual report incorporates director, executive compensation and ownership information from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so Business & governance cannot describe board composition, pay or beneficial ownership beyond the executive officers listed in the report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 47, 145

- Low: The bag-in-box product line sale, signed on 2026-10-22 and closed on 2026-11-02, is disclosed in two sentences with no price, carrying value or sales contribution. Its effect on cash, on the Packaging segment and on the post-sale perimeter cannot be quantified from the supplied sources, and it falls in no reported period.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Low: The run settings supply no peer set, dated market quotes, agency rating reports or portfolio limits, and the filings end with the third quarterly report signed on 2026-11-13, five days before the as-of date. Anything that happened between that signature and the as-of date is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C05

## Findings
### Bottom line

Total debt of USD 397.14 million is now covered by USD 1,158.54 million of cash after the March 2026 Aerospace sale, so Trimas has net cash and creditors depend on a smaller earnings base rather than on deleveraging. Derived last-twelve-month EBITDA is USD 94.74 million, which puts total debt at 4.19x and EBITDA to cash interest at 4.98x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6, 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90, 136; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03

The cushion is thinner than net cash suggests: last-twelve-month EBITDA includes a USD 35.80 million asbestos benefit booked in the fourth quarter of 2025, and without it total debt would be 6.74x EBITDA. USD 67.6 million of estimated sale tax is also still unpaid, and covenant EBITDA of USD 90.98 million is a different measure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 10, 50, 53; calculation C05

### Financial interpretation

Leverage fell from 6.43x total debt to EBITDA at the end of 2024 to 5.90x at the end of 2025 and 4.19x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net leverage moved from 6.06x to 5.52x, which becomes -10.10x pro forma for the Aerospace sale of 2026-03-16, and then to a net cash position. The first step came from EBITDA rising from USD 61.91 million to USD 79.51 million faster than debt rose from USD 398.12 million to USD 469.17 million. The second came from the Aerospace sale, which lifted cash to USD 1,158.54 million while the revolver was repaid and debt fell to USD 397.14 million. The year-end ratios set debt that funded the whole group against continuing EBITDA only, so they overstate the leverage of the business that remains, and the last-twelve-month ratio is flattered by the asbestos benefit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6, 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 88–90, 136; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C08

EBITDA to cash interest paid improved from 3.31x in 2024 to 4.24x in 2025 and 4.98x on the last twelve months. Interest paid is gross: interest income of USD 23.9 million on the sale proceeds in the nine months of 2026 exceeds interest expense of USD 13.50 million, which is why the covenant interest-cover test prints as not applicable. Interest income is outside EBITDA, so the cover ratio is unaffected by it, but the net interest burden is negative only while the proceeds stay invested; deploying the cash into acquisitions or buybacks, or a fall in rates, would remove part of that income.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation C04

Consolidated operating cash flow was USD 117.45 million in 2025 against capital expenditure of USD 48.35 million, but both include Aerospace until the sale. In the nine months of 2026 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 124.63 million, because income tax paid reached USD 132.47 million, largely on the sale gain, and receivables rose by USD 46.32 million while payables and accruals added USD 85.76 million, of which the unpaid sale tax is a large part. Cash flow for continuing operations alone is not stated, so cash conversion of the remaining business is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 10–11, 50

Liquidity is ample: cash of USD 1,158.54 million plus revolver availability of USD 243.80 million, against a maturity ladder whose only principal is the senior notes of USD 400.00 million due in 2029. The revolver is capped by leverage tests at USD 203.0 million of borrowing capacity, and the cash is invested mostly in liquid instruments such as treasury bills and money market funds while USD 67.6 million of sale tax remains payable and the company bought back USD 82.73 million of its stock in the nine months. How much of the cash is retained for acquisitions, buybacks or note repayment is a management choice the filings do not fix.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 16, 50, 54–55; calculation C06

The filings print no EBITDA, so the figure used is operating profit plus continuing depreciation and amortization, which differs from the covenant measure in perimeter, in definition and by USD 94.87 million for 2025. Covenant net leverage of 1.77x nets cash only up to USD 240.0 million, so it cannot be compared with the derived net cash position. Contract liabilities of USD 7.45 million and the absence of supplier finance, factoring or securitization mean no non-debt funding float distorts operating cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 52–54; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; calculation C07

The Aerospace sale is reported at about USD 1.45 billion in the 2025 annual report, USD 1,456.9 million in the first two quarterly reports and USD 1,457.1 million after final adjustments; the final figure serves as the price and net proceeds of USD 1,242.5 million after estimated tax and costs serve the net debt adjustment. The dividend declared on 2026-10-22 and the bag-in-box sale closed on 2026-11-02 fall after the balance sheet date, and their amounts are not stated, so they stay out of period figures.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 34; calculation C08

The strongest contrary reading is that the business is simply less levered than the year-end ratios imply: net cash of USD 761.40 million and total debt of 4.19x EBITDA on a reported basis leave ample room for acquisitions and buybacks. That reading loses weight if the asbestos benefit is excluded, because total debt is then 6.74x EBITDA, and if cash is deployed, because the earnings base of USD 94.74 million is smaller than the group that carried the debt in 2025.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 15–17; calculation C05

- High: The covenant EBITDA of USD 90.98 million and the covenant net leverage of 1.77x are on a different perimeter and definition, with cash netting capped at USD 240.0 million. They cannot support or replace the derived leverage, and covenant capacity cannot be inferred without the executed credit agreement and its amendments.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; calculation C07

- Medium: Year-end debt at 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31 funded the whole group including Aerospace, while EBITDA and the segment figures cover continuing operations only, so the two year-end leverage ratios overstate the leverage of the remaining business. A consolidated EBITDA on the pre-sale perimeter for the same years is stated only inside the covenant measure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72, 88–89; calculation C04

- Medium: Cash flow statements are consolidated and include discontinued operations until the sale, so operating cash flow, free cash flow and cash taxes for the continuing business are not stated. Depreciation, amortization and capital expenditure of discontinued operations are given in the notes and were used to separate continuing depreciation, amortization and cash capital expenditure only. A last-twelve-month operating cash flow is not calculable on a consistent basis.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 90, 105; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 11

- Medium: Net cash of USD 761.40 million is before USD 67.6 million of estimated sale tax that sits in accounts payable and before the declared dividend and any further buybacks. Restricted cash inside cash and equivalents is not separately stated, so unrestricted cash is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 10, 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 94

- Low: Printed dashes are treated as missing values, not zero. They occur for asbestos-related costs in FY2023, nine months 2026 and Q3 2026; impairment of indefinite-lived intangible assets in FY2025 and FY2023; discontinued-operations balance-sheet lines at 2026-09-30; and several cash flow lines. Reported totals remain usable; the explicit numeric disclosure would close each narrower gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6

- Low: Some line items appear in only one kind of filing, such as the impairment, environmental provision, cross-currency swap and forward settlement lines in the annual report and the asbestos estimate line in the quarterly report, so the other columns are shown as not supplied rather than zero.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

- Low: First and second quarter discrete figures for 2026 and a stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 are not extracted; the nine-month and annual figures cover the same months, and the fourth quarter could be calculated as FY2025 less nine months 2025 only on request. Per-share and share-count lines are also left out of the money tables because they are a different quantity family.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 89

- Low: The non-US revolving loan facility of USD 4.00 million has no stated rank, security, maturity or pricing, so it is left out of the debt stack and the maturity ladder. Its amount is undrawn and small.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 54

- Low: The dividend declared on 2026-10-22 has no stated total or record-date share count (the third-quarter dividend at the same rate totalled USD 1.5 million), and the bag-in-box product line sale closed on 2026-11-02 has no stated price, carrying value or sales contribution, so neither can be put into pro forma net debt. A payment ledger and the sale agreement terms would close both.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 34

- Low: The Aerospace sale price is reported three ways and the net proceeds of USD 1,242.5 million differ by USD 0.1 million from the price less stated tax and costs, a rounding difference; the final price controls and no figure is averaged.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C08

- Low: The third-quarter earnings release is not supplied, and the quarterly report lowered operating profit by USD 2.8 million after the release; the quarterly report is used and any figure that appears only in the release is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 60

- Low: Specialty Products figures include the Arrow Engine business until its sale on 2025-01-31, so comparisons across 2024, 2025 and 2026 are not like for like, and segment last-twelve-month figures are not built.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 135
- Low: The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is constructed from the instrument terms because no maturity table is printed for that date; the table printed for 2025-12-31 shows the same two instruments.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 114

spans.text: ## Request

Trimas Corp as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway: the business, transaction, ownership, operating-model and governance facts of the company after the March 2026 Aerospace sale, with sponsor and governance risk judged from the issuer's own conduct. The run supplied five SEC filings and the Source readiness analysis, and no proxy statement, executed debt document, sponsor material or transaction agreement.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (audited; date shown is the signature date) | 2026-03-02 | c89ec1527196799e2c1b72cddfd8a23815e99dc8b40fa26b95675ff706ccc8d4 | Business, segments, customers, strategy, executive officers, directors named on the signature page, Aerospace sale agreement, share repurchase authorisations and cash flows, ratings, audit reports, exhibit index and governance incorporation by reference. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited; date shown is the signature date) | 2026-11-13 | a4940df0086dc83c7f1fc8be6232362ad4c2008f9e3d14fcdf6584d018ff876a | Current segment results, sale completion, subsequent events, debt, covenant and liquidity summary, share repurchases, asbestos, ratings, earnings release adjustment and operating drivers. |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (audited; date shown is the signature date) | 2025-02-27 | c3f3c05cd2e5405b3b6b4b388602e3c7ff109ba7e0f413c1d1ed2e83aafa373c | Pre-sale three-segment perimeter and the 2024 net sales total used to test that Aerospace and continuing sales add up; no figure from it is used as current. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_trs.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended March 31, 2026 (unaudited; date shown is the signature date) | 2026-04-30 | b823fe388415b8295d300d13212a0b3a37630a0fbd49c69a5a035c0ce79ef7ff | Aerospace sale completion as first reported, first-quarter share repurchases and signature date. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_trs.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 (unaudited; date shown is the signature date) | 2026-07-31 | 933b78adaf1729293c6ad274e7dcb8a148a240575434b42383f0561160e61786 | Signature date only. |
| Supplied analysis | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 4b81bbaaa7bcdd92027ef047598529b3b785c95f9e7c4827c0754e1820d60dc7 | Source inventory, perimeter finding, documents not supplied; no business or governance fact imported without its own filing locator. |
No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Trimas is now a smaller, Packaging-led manufacturer with no controlling holder identified, and governance risk for creditors is medium: the sale cash cushions the debt, but how management deploys it is not fixed by any document supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16, 145; Source readiness (CP-0)

The business that remains is Packaging, 82.94% of 2025 net sales, plus a cylinder unit with thin margins, while the Aerospace group sold in March 2026 was 38.04% of pre-sale group net sales. After the sale the company repaid its revolver and left the USD 400.00 million 2029 notes outstanding, but it bought back USD 82.73 million of stock in the nine months to September 2026, following USD 101.10 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. Both rating agencies lowered ratings by two notches. Board independence, ownership and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so legal capacity to distribute cash or borrow is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 76, 105, 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 51, 54, 56; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C07
### Key findings

- The business that remains is smaller and more concentrated in one packaging platform. Packaging was 82.94% of 2025 net sales and 82.38% of nine-month 2026 net sales, consumer products customers took 67.49% of nine-month 2026 sales, and the Aerospace group had been 38.04% of pre-sale group net sales, so scale and diversification fell even though debt fell too.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 105, 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 27; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04

- Customer and input-cost exposure shows first in segment margins. No customer reaches 10% of consolidated net sales, but each segment has a customer above that level of its own revenue, and resin and steel costs reach prices with a lag. The cylinder unit lived through a demand trough from late 2023 to early 2025 and earned only USD 1.49 million of segment operating profit on USD 91.92 million of nine-month 2026 sales after a USD 2.1 million inventory-count charge, so one end market can erase most of a segment's profit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 27, 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 43, 47

- Ownership and control are not established beyond a widely held listing, so governance risk rests on conduct, not structure. The filings name no sponsor and no controlling holder, and the signature page lists nine directors with a separate Chairman, but independence, committee membership, consent rights and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 145, 150–151; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Leadership and policy changed in 2025 and the use of the sale cash is the main open question. A new chief executive with a packaging background joined in June 2025 and a returning chief financial officer in December 2025; the company set up a Strategic Investment Committee to weigh packaging and life sciences acquisitions against other uses of the proceeds, and management says the cash may go to organic growth, acquisitions, buybacks, dividends or repayment of debt including the notes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 16, 44, 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 57

- Documented conduct is mixed: supportive after the sale, less so before it. The company bought back USD 101.10 million of stock in the fourth quarter of 2025 while its revolver ended the year drawn at USD 72.79 million, then after the sale repaid the revolver, added no net debt and returned USD 87.13 million in nine months, 7.52% of cash at 2026-09-30; no related-party payment, priming, exchange or other liability management transaction is disclosed in the filings read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 69, 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 51, 54; calculation C06; calculation C12

- Both rating agencies lowered ratings by two notches after the sale: Moody's corporate family rating from Ba2 to B1 and S&P's corporate credit rating from BB to B+. That is the agencies' own view and not a conclusion of this analysis, and the filings do not give their reasons, but both acted after the sale was announced and neither left the earlier ratings in place despite the cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C07

- Disclosure supports monitoring with some blemishes. The annual report carries unqualified audit opinions and effective internal control, but the third-quarter earnings release was adjusted after issue, lowering operating profit by USD 2.8 million, the third quarterly report was signed 44 days after quarter end against 30 and 31 days for the first two, and the asbestos liability and its USD 32.68 million insurance recovery asset rest on management estimates.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 88, 143–144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24, 60–61; calculation C08; calculation C09
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower level is that the revolver is repaid, no net debt has been added, covenant leverage is 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum, the dividend is USD 0.04 per share a quarter, buybacks and dividends absorbed 7.52% of cash, management lists repaying debt including the notes among possible uses, and no priming, exchange or related-party transaction is disclosed. The strongest evidence for a higher level is the USD 101.10 million of buybacks before the sale closed, two authorisation increases in four months, broad discretion over the proceeds and a further fall of 1.00% in shares outstanding after quarter end. If the proxy statement shows an independent board and no controlling holder, and the executed documents restrict distributions and new debt tightly, the level would move to low. It would move to high if the cash is spent on debt-funded acquisitions, special distributions or a much larger buyback, or if the credit agreement is amended to widen restricted-payment capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 53, 55, 57; calculation C06; calculation C11
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, compensation design and beneficial ownership are not established; the medium level therefore rests on issuer conduct alone and cannot be lowered on governance structure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 145

- The executed credit agreement and notes indenture are not supplied, so the size of the restricted-payment, investment and debt baskets cannot be separated from management's willingness, and a low or high assessment of financial policy would need those documents.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 146–150; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

- Management's stated priorities for the sale cash are known only from the annual and quarterly reports, because the third-quarter earnings release and any investor presentation are not supplied; any later announcement of an acquisition or a larger buyback would change the assessment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 57, 60
### Governance view

Overall, Trimas presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The risk level is driven by USD 101.10 million of buybacks before the sale closed, USD 87.13 million of buybacks and dividends in nine months of 2026 and a management plan that leaves the use of USD 1,158.54 million of cash open, because cash that is returned or spent on acquisitions is no longer available to the holders of the USD 400.00 million unsecured notes, which implies that creditor risk moves with how much of the cash is returned or spent. Countervailing evidence is the repaid revolver, no net new debt, reported total net leverage of 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum and the absence of any extraction, related-party or liability management event. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and any announced acquisition. Business & governance completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 53; calculation C06; calculation C12

spans.text: ## Request

Trimas Corp as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway: the fundamental credit profile of the company after the March 2026 Aerospace sale, its strongest support, its weakest material dimension and its primary downside path. The analysis rests on five SEC filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses, with no peer data, executed debt document or management presentation supplied.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Trimas has adequate credit quality for its USD 400.00 million unsecured 2029 notes: cash covers the principal 2.90 times and nothing matures before April 2029, but the earnings base behind the notes is small and the use of the cash is open.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 94.74 million falls to USD 58.94 million without a one-off asbestos benefit, and 68.09% of nine-month pre-tax income came from interest on the sale cash, so spending the cash would weaken earnings as well as the cushion. The Specialty Products cylinder unit earns thin margins, while Packaging supplies 97.19% of segment profit. Both rating agencies lowered ratings by two notches, and the executed debt documents are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 56; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05
### Key findings

- Liquidity is the credit's main support and removes refinancing pressure before April 2029. Cash of USD 1,158.54 million and revolver availability of USD 243.80 million sit against the USD 400.00 million of notes as the only debt, so cash alone covers the principal 2.90 times, or 2.73 times after the USD 67.6 million of estimated sale tax still payable; revolver capacity is already cut to USD 203.00 million by leverage restrictions, which shows the smaller earnings base limits borrowing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16, 50, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C12

- The earnings base is the weak point. Reported last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 94.74 million includes a USD 35.80 million asbestos benefit, 37.79% of it, so total debt is 4.19x EBITDA as reported and 6.74x without the benefit, and EBITDA covers cash interest 4.98x as reported and 3.10x without it; covenant EBITDA, which still carried Aerospace for 2025, fell 47.83% from USD 174.38 million to USD 90.98 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72, 89; calculation C02; calculation C03

- Earnings quality leans on interest income from the sale cash. Interest income was USD 23.9 million in nine months, 68.09% of pre-tax income of USD 35.10 million, and 75.91% of the third quarter's, so pre-tax income without it would have been USD 11.20 million; at the stated 3.9% average rate each USD 100.00 million of cash deployed removes about USD 3.90 million of annual income.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 27, 46, 55; calculation C04

- Packaging anchors the credit and Specialty Products weighs on it. Packaging earned 97.19% of segment operating profit in nine months at an 11.98% margin, down from 13.17%, with organic sales growth of 8.2% in the third quarter, while Specialty Products earned a 1.62% margin and lost money in the third quarter after an inventory-count charge and production inefficiencies; cylinder gross margin fell 3.5 percentage points to 5.5%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 41–43, 47; calculation C05; calculation C07

- Input costs stay exposed but cost actions offset part of the risk. Resin, steel and aluminum prices reach customers with a lag and tariffs raised Packaging input costs in 2025, and in nine months of 2026 Packaging gross margin fell 0.7 percentage points to 23.4% after higher realignment costs; management expects annualised savings of about USD 15.00 million from the 2026 realignment, 15.83% of last-twelve-month EBITDA, and corporate expense fell to 50.04% of segment profit from 79.71%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 55, 59, 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38, 47–49; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

- Capital allocation is the swing factor and conduct is mixed. The company bought back USD 101.10 million of stock in the fourth quarter of 2025 with its revolver drawn, then repaid the revolver after the sale and returned USD 87.13 million in nine months of 2026, 7.52% of cash, against USD 2.26 million a year earlier; management lists repaying debt including the notes among possible uses but prioritises growth investment, acquisitions and buybacks.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 76–77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 55, 57; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

- Cash conversion of the remaining business is not established. Cash capital expenditure of USD 17.54 million over the last twelve months is 2.59% of net sales and EBITDA less that spending covers cash interest 4.06x, but the cash flow statements are consolidated and nine-month operating cash flow was an outflow because of sale tax, so free cash flow cannot be stated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 27; calculation C09

- The notes sit behind secured debt and the non-guarantor subsidiaries. The undrawn secured revolver ranks ahead of the unsecured notes, subsidiaries that do not guarantee them generated 38% of net sales so guarantors generated 62%, and Moody's and S&P each lowered ratings by two notches after the sale.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 51, 56; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger view is that the company has net cash of USD 761.40 million, no maturity before April 2029, reported covenant leverage of 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum and cost savings of about USD 15.00 million a year still to come, which would make adequate too cautious if the cash stays on the balance sheet. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that without the asbestos benefit total debt is 6.74x EBITDA and interest income supplies 68.09% of pre-tax income. The view would improve if EBITDA without one-off items reaches the reported level on its own, if the notes are repaid or the cash is retained, or if Specialty Products returns to a positive margin. It would weaken if cash is spent on debt-funded acquisitions or a much larger buyback, if the revolver is drawn, if Packaging organic growth turns negative, or if the cylinder losses of the third quarter recur.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27, 53, 55, 57; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C08
### Limitations

- Cash flow of the continuing business is not stated, because the statements are consolidated and include Aerospace until the sale, so the adequate view of cash-flow durability rests on EBITDA less capital expenditure and cannot be confirmed against free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6

- No peer, market share or sector benchmark is supplied, so the competitive position and the cost position behind the margin conclusions come from the issuer's own descriptions and could be better or worse against competitors.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

- The debt documents that would show whether acquisitions or distributions may be funded with debt are not supplied, so the primary downside path is described without a test of what the company is permitted to do and the triggers rest on reported ratios.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are liquidity, a stable packaging franchise and low capital intensity. Cash of USD 1,158.54 million and revolver availability of USD 243.80 million cover the USD 400.00 million of notes 2.90 times on cash alone, with no maturity before April 2029. Packaging earns 97.19% of segment operating profit at an 11.98% margin with third-quarter organic growth of 8.2%, and last-twelve-month cash capital expenditure of USD 17.54 million is 2.59% of net sales, so spending can be flexed. The revolver was repaid after the sale and reported covenant leverage is 1.77x against a 4.00x maximum.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16, 27, 41, 53; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C09

The main weaknesses are a small and partly one-off earnings base, dependence on interest income and an open capital allocation policy. EBITDA of USD 94.74 million includes a USD 35.80 million asbestos benefit, interest income is 68.09% of nine-month pre-tax income, and Specialty Products earns a 1.62% margin. Management has not fixed the use of the cash, bought back USD 101.10 million of stock before the sale closed, and the unsecured notes rank behind the undrawn secured revolver and the non-guarantor subsidiaries.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 55, 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 50; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05
### Company description

Trimas makes dispensing and closure systems for consumer products, life sciences and industrial customers, which are 82.94% of net sales, and steel cylinders for industrial gas, health care and defense uses, which are 17.06%. The Aerospace group, which was 38.04% of pre-sale group net sales, was sold in March 2026 and the bag-in-box product line followed in November 2026. Many Packaging products are designed to customer specifications, and the footprint across North America, Europe and Asia lets customers buy locally, which supports retention but also exposes the company to the buying patterns of large consumer brands. The credit linkage is that the remaining business is smaller but steadier: Packaging net sales rose in 2024, in 2025 and in nine months of 2026 while the cylinder unit has swung with industrial demand, so debt service rests on one platform with two end-market risks.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12, 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05
### Ownership and group structure

Trimas is a widely held NASDAQ company with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so ownership adds no documented sponsor-extraction risk but also no sponsor support, and financial policy rests on the board and a new management team. A new chief executive joined in June 2025 and a chief financial officer in December 2025, a Strategic Investment Committee evaluates acquisitions and other uses of the sale cash, and the notes are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries only, so a share of earnings sits outside the guarantee. The governance risk level from Business & governance is medium, which this analysis adopts: conduct has been mixed and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 48, 145; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is spread across consumer, life sciences and industrial customers but is cyclical at the edges. Packaging net sales grew 5.8% in nine months of 2026, with life sciences up USD 13.5 million and dispensing for beauty and personal care up USD 4.4 million, partly offset by a USD 5.1 million fall in other consumer goods, and organic growth reached 8.2% in the third quarter. The cylinder unit's sales rose 9.5% on industrial demand and market share gains after a demand trough from late 2023 to early 2025. Pricing power is limited: price increases generally lag input costs, escalator clauses exist only in some contracts, and each segment has a customer above 10% of its revenue, so order changes by one buyer can move segment results. Recent growth supports near-term revenue, but contract duration and renewal data are not supplied, so visibility beyond the next year and any pricing cushion against cost shocks are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 41–42, 46–47
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins have held in Packaging and not in Specialty Products. Packaging gross margin was 23.4% in nine months of 2026 against 24.1%, after USD 1.9 million of higher realignment costs from closing one facility, having already fallen in 2025 on higher input costs including tariffs, and its segment margin was 11.98% against 13.17%. In Specialty Products, a USD 2.1 million inventory-count charge, machine downtime and labour inefficiency cut the gross margin from 9.0% to 5.5%. Resin, steel and aluminum are the largest purchases and price increases lag cost increases, so a cost shock first hits margin and then cash conversion. Corporate expense fell to USD 26.50 million from USD 44.64 million, partly because a USD 8.0 million asbestos charge in the prior year did not repeat. Packaging segment margin held between 12.72% and 13.30% across 2023 to 2025, so margins have been defended through volume and cost swings so far, but a cost shock in resin or steel would pass through to EBITDA with a delay.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 55, 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 41–43, 45, 47–49; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low and flexible: cash capital expenditure of continuing operations was USD 17.54 million over the last twelve months, 2.59% of net sales, against USD 31.69 million in 2025, so EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest 4.06x. Against that, receivables rose USD 46.32 million in nine months and days sales outstanding rose twelve days because sales grew with customers that pay more slowly, and realignment, severance and system costs continue. Taxes on the sale gain, not operations, drove the nine-month operating cash outflow. EBITDA therefore appears to convert into cash for debt service, but the conversion of the remaining business cannot be measured until a continuing cash flow statement exists.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 27, 50; calculation C09
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is moderate: no single competitor matches the whole Packaging range, but Amcor, Aptar, Silgan, Greif, Bericap and smaller Asian producers compete in each product line, so the main margin risk is the lag in passing on cost increases rather than a stated price war. Buyer power is high for the large consumer brands that are the main customers, because the company says they may seek lower prices, different payment terms or local supply, and each segment has a customer above 10% of its revenue. Supplier power is low to moderate: resins are commodities with several suppliers, while steel is bought from mills and service centers and has had supply and pricing challenges, so supplier terms matter less than the lag in passing costs on. The threat of substitutes and of new entrants is not established from the materials supplied; the company notes only that customers may diversify their supply base and that sustainability goals push design toward less material.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 16, 27
### PEST analysis

Economic and political factors are material to credit; social and technological factors are not a primary driver on the materials supplied. Tariffs imposed on inputs raised Packaging costs in 2025 and the company states that future tariffs and trade actions are uncertain, geopolitical conflict in the Middle East may raise raw material costs and affect the fourth quarter, and currency effects moved nine-month net sales by USD 9.7 million. Each factor works through input costs and pricing lag, which compress margin before they reach cash, and the company hedges currency with forward and swap contracts on a notional USD 120.6 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 55, 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 56–57
### SWOT analysis

Strengths: liquidity of USD 1,402.34 million against USD 400.00 million of notes, a packaging franchise with an 11.98% segment margin, low capital intensity, and a repaid revolver. Weaknesses: a USD 58.94 million earnings base without the asbestos benefit, a cylinder unit with a 1.62% margin, interest income that is 68.09% of pre-tax income, and unsecured notes behind secured debt. Opportunities: realignment savings of about USD 15.00 million a year, life sciences growth and acquisitions in packaging that add earnings if they are paid for from cash. Threats: debt-funded acquisitions or large buybacks, cost shocks that outrun pricing, a fall in interest rates or cash deployment that removes interest income, and further rating action.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16, 27, 46, 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 76; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04
### Financial profile and credit quality

The credit supports are liquidity, the absence of maturities before 2029 and a margin-stable packaging platform; the constraints are the small earnings base, interest income dependence and an open financial policy. The trend is favourable on leverage, with total debt to EBITDA falling from 6.43x at the end of 2024 to 5.90x at the end of 2025 and 4.19x on the last twelve months, but that trend rests on debt that funded Aerospace, on EBITDA that includes a one-off benefit and on net cash created by a sale. Total debt without the asbestos benefit is 6.74x EBITDA, so the underlying deleveraging is smaller than the headline. The key missing datapoints are free cash flow of the continuing business, management's adjusted EBITDA, the executed debt documents and sector benchmarks.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C13
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are life sciences growth, third-quarter organic growth of 8.2% in Packaging and realignment savings of more than USD 10 million in 2026 that rise to about USD 15.00 million annualised, with management saying the third quarter did not yet reflect them. The headwinds are cylinder throughput problems that management calls temporary, raw material and tariff costs, the payment of the USD 67.6 million of estimated sale tax, lower interest income if rates fall or cash is deployed, and the fourth quarter, which is usually the seasonal low. Over three to five years the issuer's plan is a one-company packaging model with acquisitions in packaging and life sciences, which could raise earnings but is the main way leverage and cash could change course; the outlook for the notes depends more on that policy than on operations.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19, 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 41, 50, 55, 57; calculation C04; calculation C08
### Downside scenario

The most credible downside is a policy-led one, not an operating collapse. If management spends most of the sale cash on acquisitions and buybacks while consumer demand softens and resin, steel or tariff costs outrun pricing, Packaging gross margin would fall further from the 23.4% of nine months 2026 and the cylinder unit would keep losing money, as in the third quarter. EBITDA would then move toward the USD 58.94 million that remains without the asbestos benefit, interest income would fall by about USD 3.90 million a year for every USD 100.00 million deployed, and total debt to EBITDA would stand at 6.74x even with no new debt. If acquisitions or buybacks were funded with the revolver, secured debt would rank ahead of the notes and borrowing capacity of USD 203.00 million, already limited by leverage tests, could shrink as covenant EBITDA falls. The notes would face refinancing in April 2029 at a lower rating on a smaller earnings base. Management levers are cutting buybacks, lowering capital expenditure from a low base and using the cash to repay the notes. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months, because cash alone covers the notes 2.90 times; distress would need a large cash outflow and a deep earnings fall together. The first observable signals are a falling cash balance, a drawn revolver, negative Packaging organic growth and repeated cylinder losses.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16, 43, 47, 53–55; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C07; calculation C12
### Overall credit view

Overall, Trimas presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity that covers the notes 2.90 times and a margin-stable Packaging franchise, but credit quality is constrained by a small earnings base of USD 94.74 million that includes a one-off benefit, earnings that lean on interest income, and an open capital allocation policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but not fully assessable, because EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest 4.06x while free cash flow of the continuing business is not stated. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how much cash is retained until April 2029 and on EBITDA without one-off items. The primary downside path is a cash- or revolver-funded acquisition or buyback program at the same time as cylinder losses and input-cost pressure. Further analysis would require a continuing cash flow statement, management's adjusted EBITDA, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and sector benchmarks. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: use of the sale cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27, 55, 57; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C09

## Gaps

- High: Free cash flow of the continuing business is not stated because the cash flow statements are consolidated and include Aerospace until the sale. Cash-flow durability is therefore judged from EBITDA and capital expenditure, and a continuing cash flow statement would let the view move to strong or weak.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 6

- High: The executed credit agreement and notes indenture are not supplied, so whether acquisitions, buybacks or secured borrowing are limited, and by how much, is not established. This limits the downside scenario and the monitoring triggers to reported ratios.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

- Medium: Management's adjusted EBITDA and the third-quarter earnings release are not supplied, so EBITDA is the derived figure including the asbestos benefit and the sensitivity without it is an analyst calculation.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 60
- Medium: Peer, market share and sector data are not supplied, so competitive advantage, new entrants and the sector outlook are described from the issuer's own statements only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12
- Medium: Customers at or above 10% of segment revenue are not named, and contract duration, renewal and churn are not stated, so revenue visibility and customer power cannot be sized.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 27
- Low: The rating agencies' reports are not supplied, so the reasons for the downgrades are not established and the filings state only the rating levels.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trs.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 56
- Low: The price of the bag-in-box sale and the total of the October 2026 dividend are not stated, so their cash effect is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 34
- Low: Events after the third quarterly report signed on 2026-11-13 are not covered, so any acquisition, buyback or financing since then is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trs.htm.jsonl, page 61; Source readiness (CP-0)
